title: Topology-aware capacity reservation with zonal prefetch and soft spillback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a topology-aware reservation and soft-spillback mechanism for regional/multi-zone dedicated fleets. The feature should allow per-customer capacity commitments to be sliced across zones with prioritized local serving, proactive zonal prefetching when occupancy is high, and controlled soft spillback to other zones/regions while honoring data-residency tags. Goal: preserve throughput guarantees and improve graceful degradation without violating residency constraints or significantly increasing tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment slices can be created and inspected per-customer with zone affinity metadata
Autoscaler respects slice boundaries and can prefetch a 10% buffer to adjacent zones when local utilization > 80%
Soft spillback routes up to configured spillback_percent (default 15%) while preserving residency-tagged requests locally or to approved fallback locations
Observability: dashboards for slice utilization, spillback events, per-zone tail latency (p95/p99), and throughput loss during failover
Canaries show no regression in median latency and <10% increase in p99 under simulated single-zone drain scenarios
Security: KMS-integrated audit log entries created for any cross-zone spillback decision affecting residency-sensitive customers
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Data model and API (2 weeks) - extend commitment model to include zone slices and residency tags. Phase 2: Runtime routing + prefetch (3 weeks) - implement lightweight prefetch engine that warms KV cache / prewarmed workers in adjacent zones based on occupancy signals. Phase 3: Soft spillback policy + enforcement (2 weeks) - implement policy engine that evaluates spillback_percent, residency allowlist, and rate limits. Phase 4: Observability, tests, and rollout (2 weeks). Use feature flags to gate each capability.
testing_plan: Unit tests for slice allocation and policy logic; integration tests with autoscaler simulation; chaos test: scheduled single-zone drain and simulated network partition; load test: multi-tenant synthetic workload with mixed residency tags to validate spillback caps and throughput guarantees; security test: verify audit events and KMS access flows.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary on non-residency customers in a single region. 2) Gradual ramp to 10% of dedicated fleets with feature flag. 3) Enable residency-aware checks for selected pilot customers (opt-in) and run acceptance suite. 4) Full rollout with monitoring thresholds and automatic rollback if p99 increases > 25% or customer errors increase > 2x.

risks: Incorrect residency tag handling could cause regulatory exposure if requests are routed to non-authorized zones
Aggressive prefetching increases cost if heuristics are poorly tuned
Spillback decisions may increase tail latency for affected requests
Complexity in autoscaler integration could cause oscillation between zones under flapping signals
perf_targets: Maintain median latency within 5% of baseline for committed traffic
p95 increase <= 10% during single-zone drain under expected load
Maintain >= 95% of committed throughput for residency-tagged traffic within region
Spillback rate <= configured spillback_percent (default 15%) in steady-state
